proofUses.reason: Facial cycle constraints identify finite-support rooted diagrams; facewise Holder and positive Fejer approximations bound the critical sums.
The expanded strip has faces of length at most six and two edge-disjoint outer routes; mixed L3/L12 norms retain at least N-2 small connectors.
The critical infrared bound makes the unweighted connector L12 norm small; repeated doubling supplies fixed moments, spatial derivative bounds and a fourth-order Taylor remainder.
Exact real-weight densities give the two marked L3 factors; all placements retain the small connector factors, with Parseval at order zero and a direct bound at order one.
Dyadic gains first supply the desired real input moment; one real-order gain reaches any output strictly below 2(d-6)/3, with weighted continuity and spatial decay.
Integrate the block faces first; every remaining connector face then has at most four factors, giving marked L^(18/7) and unmarked L9 bounds.
The two-route distribution and exact moment densities double K under (18/7)(K+2)<d; the fixed-kernel iteration reaches s<7d/9-4.
Each marked connector-block transition has row sum bounded by two weighted triangle norms; unmarked transitions retain T times Delta. The two outer-route marks affect at most two transitions.

Exact input-moment convolution bounds give the weighted triangles when 2K+6<d. Iteration from the second moment reaches every s<d-6 under the fixed small-triangle condition, without assuming Gaussian decay.
